name: Workshop — Lambda + API Gateway
description: L2 constructs, the asset pipeline, and the IAM wiring the framework derives for you.

inputSteps.title: L2 construct imports
inputSteps.content: The same L2 vocabulary as AWS CDK — typed classes with behaviour, not modules with variables.

inputSteps.title: Extending AwsStack
inputSteps.content: AwsStack owns the asset pipeline, the IAM model, and region/partition lookups. Anything constructed inside it reaches those services through the tree.

inputSteps.title: A function, not a folder of variables
inputSteps.content: Code.fromAsset() hands the bundle to the asset pipeline. The construct decides how it is hashed, packaged and referenced — you never write that plumbing.

inputSteps.title: Passing an object, not a string
inputSteps.content: handler: hello passes the function itself. LambdaRestApi asks it for an invoke ARN and grants itself permission. That handshake is why nothing outside these two constructs has to wire them together.

outputSteps.title: Trust policy, derived
outputSteps.content: The Lambda service principal is resolved through a data source instead of hardcoded, so the same program synthesizes correctly in any partition.

outputSteps.title: The asset pipeline, in plain Terraform
outputSteps.content: Bucket, object, content hash and source path — all emitted from that one Code.fromAsset() call, all managed by ordinary Terraform state.

outputSteps.title: Race conditions, pre-solved
outputSteps.content: Explicit depends_on, create_before_destroy, and a redeployment trigger hashed from the API definition. This is the part of a hand-written module that is always subtly wrong.

outputSteps.title: Cross-service permission you never asked for
outputSteps.content: You never wrote a lambda_permission. The API construct asked the function for a grant, and it materialized here with the correct source ARN.
